title_en: Regulations on the Disclosure of Government Information of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of safeguarding the rights of citizens, legal persons and other organizations to obtain government information according to law, enhancing the transparency of government work, building a law-based government, and giving full play to the service role of government information in the production, life and economic and social activities of the people.

Article 2 For the purposes of these Regulations, "government information" means the information produced or obtained by administrative organs in the course of performing their administrative management functions, which is recorded and preserved in a certain form.

Article 3 The people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the organizational leadership of government information disclosure work.
The General Office of the State Council is the competent department for government information disclosure work nationwide, responsible for promoting, guiding, coordinating and supervising the government information disclosure work nationwide.
The general offices (offices) of local people's governments at or above the county level are the competent departments for government information disclosure work in their respective administrative regions, responsible for promoting, guiding, coordinating and supervising the government information disclosure work in their respective administrative regions.
The general offices (offices) of departments under vertical leadership shall be in charge of the government information disclosure work of their respective systems.

Article 5 Administrative organs shall adhere to the principle that disclosure is the norm and non-disclosure is the exception, and shall follow the principles of justice, fairness, legality and convenience to the people in disclosing government information.

Article 6 Administrative organs shall disclose government information in a timely and accurate manner.
Where an administrative organ discovers false or incomplete information that affects or may affect social stability, or disrupts social and economic management order, it shall publish accurate government information to clarify.
Article 7 The people's governments at all levels shall actively promote government information disclosure work, and gradually increase the content of government information disclosure.

Article 8 The people's governments at all levels shall strengthen the standardized, standardized and information-based management of government information resources, strengthen the construction of Internet government information disclosure platforms, promote the integration of government information disclosure platforms and government service platforms, and improve the online handling level of government information disclosure.
Article 9 Citizens, legal persons and other organizations shall have the right to supervise the government information disclosure work of administrative organs and to make criticisms and suggestions.

Article 10 Government information produced by an administrative organ shall be disclosed by the administrative organ that produced it. Government information obtained by an administrative organ from citizens, legal persons or other organizations shall be disclosed by the administrative organ that preserves it; government information obtained by an administrative organ from another administrative organ shall be disclosed by the administrative organ that produced or first obtained it. Where laws or regulations otherwise provide for the authority to disclose government information, such provisions shall prevail.
Where the dispatched agencies or internal institutions established by an administrative organ perform administrative management functions externally in their own name in accordance with laws or regulations, such dispatched agencies or internal institutions may be responsible for the disclosure of government information related to the administrative management functions they perform.
Government information jointly produced by two or more administrative organs shall be disclosed by the administrative organ that takes the lead in producing it.

Article 11 Administrative organs shall establish and improve the coordination mechanism for government information disclosure. Where the government information disclosed by an administrative organ involves other organs, it shall consult and confirm with the relevant organs to ensure that the government information disclosed by the administrative organ is accurate and consistent.
Where the disclosure of government information by an administrative organ requires approval in accordance with laws, administrative regulations or relevant state provisions, it shall be disclosed after approval.

Article 12 The government information disclosure guide and government information disclosure catalogue compiled and published by an administrative organ shall be updated in a timely manner.
The government information disclosure guide includes the classification, arrangement system, access methods of government information and the name, office address, office hours, contact telephone number, fax number, Internet contact information, etc. of the government information disclosure working institution.
The government information disclosure catalogue includes the index, name, content summary, generation date, etc. of government information.

Article 13 Except for government information specified in Articles 14, 15 and 16 of these Regulations, government information shall be disclosed.
Administrative organs shall disclose government information through proactive disclosure and disclosure upon application.

Article 14 Government information that is determined as state secrets according to law, government information the disclosure of which is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations, and government information that may endanger national security, public security, economic security or social stability after disclosure shall not be disclosed.

Article 15 An administrative organ shall not disclose government information that involves trade secrets, personal privacy, etc., the disclosure of which may harm the legitimate rights and interests of a third party. However, if the third party consents to the disclosure or the administrative organ considers that non-disclosure may cause a significant impact on the public interest, it shall be disclosed.

Article 16 Internal affairs information of an administrative organ, including information on personnel management, logistics management, internal work processes, etc., may not be disclosed.
Procedural information such as discussion records, drafts, consultation letters, request-for-instruction reports, etc., formed in the course of an administrative organ's performance of administrative management functions, as well as administrative law enforcement case file information, may not be disclosed. Where laws, regulations or rules provide that the above information shall be disclosed, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 17 Administrative organs shall establish and improve the review mechanism for government information disclosure, and specify the procedures and responsibilities for review.
Administrative organs shall review government information to be disclosed in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on Guarding State Secrets and other laws, regulations and relevant state provisions.
Where an administrative organ cannot determine whether government information may be disclosed, it shall, in accordance with laws, regulations and relevant state provisions, report to the relevant competent department or the administrative department for secrecy to determine.

Article 18 Administrative organs shall establish and improve a dynamic adjustment mechanism for government information management, conduct regular evaluation and review of government information that is not disclosed by the administrative organ, and shall disclose government information that may be disclosed due to changes in circumstances.

Article 19 Administrative organs shall proactively disclose government information that concerns the adjustment of public interests, requires broad public awareness or requires public participation in decision-making.

Article 21 In addition to the government information prescribed in Article 20 of these Regulations, the people's governments of cities divided into districts and of counties and their departments shall, based on their local specific circumstances, proactively disclose government information concerning municipal construction, public services, public welfare undertakings, land acquisition, house expropriation, public security management, social assistance, and other aspects; the people's governments of townships (towns) shall, based on their local specific circumstances, proactively disclose government information concerning the implementation and carry-out of agriculture, rural areas and farmers policies, the construction and operation of farmland water conservancy projects, the transfer of rural land contractual management rights, the review of homestead use, land acquisition, house expropriation, fund-raising and labor pooling, social assistance, and other aspects.

Article 22 An administrative organ shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 20 and Article 21 of these Regulations, determine the specific content of government information to be proactively disclosed, and shall, in accordance with the arrangements of the superior administrative organ, continuously increase the content of proactive disclosure.

Article 23 An administrative organ shall establish and improve a government information release mechanism, and shall disclose the government information to be proactively disclosed via such channels as the government gazette, the government website or other internet-based government media, press conferences, and newspapers and periodicals, radio, television, etc.

Article 24 People's governments at all levels shall strengthen the work of disclosing government information through government portal websites, and shall use a unified government information disclosure platform to centrally publish proactively disclosed government information. The government information disclosure platform shall have functions such as information search, browsing, and downloading.

Article 25 People's governments at all levels shall set up government information inspection places in the national archives, public libraries, and government service venues, and shall be equipped with corresponding facilities and equipment to facilitate citizens, legal persons and other organizations in accessing government information.
Administrative organs may, as needed, establish places and facilities such as public reading rooms, material pickup points, information bulletin boards, and electronic information screens to disclose government information.
Administrative organs shall promptly provide the national archives and public libraries with proactively disclosed government information.

Article 26 Government information falling within the scope of proactive disclosure shall be promptly disclosed within 20 working days from the date on which the government information is formed or changed. Where laws or regulations have other provisions on the time limit for government information disclosure, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 27 In addition to the government information proactively disclosed by administrative organs, citizens, legal persons or other organizations may apply to the local people's governments at all levels and the departments of the people's governments at or above the county level that perform administrative management functions in their own name externally (including the dispatched agencies and internal organs as prescribed in Article 10, paragraph 2 of these Regulations) for access to relevant government information.

Article 28 The administrative organs as prescribed in Article 27 of these Regulations shall establish and improve the channels for government information disclosure applications, and shall facilitate applicants in applying for access to government information according to law.

Article 30 Where the content of a government information disclosure application is unclear, the administrative organ shall provide guidance and clarification, and shall, within 7 working days from the date of receipt of the application, inform the applicant at one time to make a supplement or correction, stating the matters requiring supplement or correction and a reasonable time limit for supplement or correction. The time limit for response shall be calculated from the date on which the administrative organ receives the supplemented or corrected application. Where the applicant fails to make the supplement or correction within the time limit without legitimate reason, the application shall be deemed to be abandoned, and the administrative organ shall no longer process the government information disclosure application.

Article 32 Where disclosure of government information upon application would harm the lawful rights and interests of a third party, the administrative organ shall solicit the opinion of the third party in writing. The third party shall provide its opinion within 15 working days from the date of receipt of the consultation letter. Where the third party fails to provide its opinion within the time limit, the administrative organ shall decide whether to disclose the information in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations. Where the third party does not agree to disclose and has reasonable grounds, the administrative organ shall not disclose the information. Where the administrative organ considers that nondisclosure may cause a significant impact on the public interest, it may decide to disclose the information, and shall notify the third party in writing of the content of the government information decided to be disclosed and the reasons.

Article 33 Where the administrative organ, upon receipt of a government information disclosure application, can respond on the spot, it shall respond on the spot.
Where the administrative organ cannot respond on the spot, it shall respond within 20 working days from the date of receipt of the application; where an extension of the response period is necessary, the extension shall be subject to the consent of the person in charge of the government information disclosure working body and the applicant shall be informed, and the extended period shall not exceed 20 working days at most.
The time required for the administrative organ to solicit opinions from the third party and other organs shall not be counted in the time limit prescribed in the preceding paragraph.

Article 34 Where the government information applied for disclosure is jointly produced by two or more administrative organs, the lead producing administrative organ may, after receiving the government information disclosure application, solicit opinions from the relevant administrative organs. The solicited organ shall provide its opinion within 15 working days from the date of receipt of the consultation letter, and failure to provide an opinion within the time limit shall be deemed to agree to the disclosure.

Article 35 Where the quantity or frequency of government information disclosure applications made by an applicant obviously exceeds a reasonable scope, the administrative organ may request the applicant to state the reasons. Where the administrative organ considers the reasons for the application to be unreasonable, it shall inform the applicant that the application shall not be processed; where the administrative organ considers the reasons to be reasonable but cannot respond to the applicant within the time limit prescribed in Article 33 of these Regulations, it may determine a reasonable period for delayed response and inform the applicant.

Article 37 Where the information applied for contains content that shall not be disclosed or does not constitute government information, but can be processed separately, the administrative organ shall provide to the applicant the content of the government information that can be disclosed, and state the reasons for the content that is not disclosed.

Article 38 The information provided by the administrative organ to the applicant shall be government information that has already been produced or obtained. Except where separate processing can be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Article 37 of these Regulations, where it is necessary for the administrative organ to process or analyze existing government information, the administrative organ may not provide such information.

Article 39 Where an applicant carries out activities such as petitions, complaints or reports in the form of a government information disclosure application, the administrative organ shall inform the applicant that the application shall not be treated as a government information disclosure application and may inform the applicant of submitting through corresponding channels.
Where the content of an application submitted by an applicant is to request the administrative organ to provide publicly published materials such as the government gazette, newspapers, periodicals, or books, the administrative organ may inform the applicant of the channels for obtaining them.

Article 40 Where an administrative organ discloses government information upon application, it shall determine the specific form for providing the government information based on the applicant's request and the actual situation of the government information stored by the administrative organ; if providing the government information in the form requested by the applicant may endanger the safety of the government information carrier or involve excessive disclosure cost, the information may be provided through electronic data or other appropriate forms, or the applicant may be arranged to inspect or copy the relevant government information.

Article 41 A citizen, legal person, or any other organization that has evidence proving that a government information record provided by an administrative organ relating to itself is inaccurate may request the administrative organ to make corrections. If the administrative organ with the authority to make corrections verifies the facts, it shall make the correction and notify the applicant; if it is not within the functions of this administrative organ, the administrative organ may transfer the matter to the administrative organ with the authority to make corrections for handling and notify the applicant, or notify the applicant to submit the request to the administrative organ with the authority to make corrections.

Article 42 An administrative organ that provides government information upon application shall not charge any fees. However, if the quantity or frequency of applications submitted by the applicant for disclosure of government information clearly exceeds a reasonable scope, the administrative organ may charge information processing fees.
The specific measures for the administrative organ to charge information processing fees shall be formulated by the competent price department of the State Council in conjunction with the finance department of the State Council and the competent department of national government information disclosure work.
Article 43 If a citizen applying for disclosure of government information has reading difficulties or audiovisual impairments, the administrative organ shall provide necessary assistance to them.

Article 44 If multiple applicants submit applications for disclosure of the same government information to the same administrative organ, and the government information is subject to disclosure, the administrative organ may include it in the scope of proactive disclosure.
With respect to government information disclosed by an administrative organ upon application, if the applicant believes that it involves adjustments to public interests, requires broad public awareness, or requires public participation in decision-making, the applicant may suggest that the administrative organ include the information in the scope of proactive disclosure. If the administrative organ, upon verification, considers that the information falls within the scope of proactive disclosure, it shall promptly disclose it proactively.

Article 45 An administrative organ shall establish and improve a working system for registration, review, processing, response, and archiving of government information disclosure applications, and shall enhance work norms.

Article 46 People's governments at all levels shall establish and improve an assessment system for government information disclosure work, a social appraisal system, and an accountability system, and shall regularly assess and appraise the government information disclosure work.

Article 47 The competent department of government information disclosure work shall strengthen daily guidance and supervision over government information disclosure work. For administrative organs that fail to carry out government information disclosure work in accordance with the requirements, it shall urge them to make corrections or issue a notice of criticism; where it is necessary to investigate the responsibility of the responsible leaders and directly responsible personnel, it shall, according to law, submit suggestions for handling to the competent authority.
If a citizen, legal person, or any other organization believes that an administrative organ fails to proactively disclose government information in accordance with the requirements or fails to respond to and handle government information disclosure applications according to law, it may submit a complaint to the competent department of government information disclosure work. If the competent department of government information disclosure work verifies the facts, it shall urge the administrative organ to make corrections or issue a notice of criticism.

Article 48 The competent department of government information disclosure work shall conduct regular training for the personnel of administrative organs responsible for government information disclosure work.

Article 49 A department of a people's government at or above the county level shall, before January 31 of each year, submit to the competent department of government information disclosure work at the same level the annual report on government information disclosure work of the preceding year of this administrative organ and shall make it public.
The competent department of government information disclosure work of a local people's government at or above the county level shall, before March 31 of each year, make public the annual report on government information disclosure work of the preceding year of the government at the same level.

Article 51 If a citizen, legal person, or any other organization believes that an administrative organ infringes upon its lawful rights and interests in government information disclosure work, it may complain or report to the administrative organ at the next higher level or the competent department of government information disclosure work, and may also apply for administrative reconsideration or file an administrative action according to law.

Article 52 If an administrative organ violates the provisions of these Regulations and fails to establish and improve the relevant systems and mechanisms for government information disclosure, the administrative organ at the next higher level shall order it to make corrections; if the circumstances are serious, the responsible leaders and directly responsible personnel shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 54 These Regulations shall apply to the activities of organizations authorized by laws and regulations to exercise the function of managing public affairs in disclosing government information.

Article 55 Public enterprises and institutions closely related to the interests of the people, such as education, health, water supply, power supply, gas supply, heat supply, environmental protection, and public transportation, that disclose information produced or obtained in the process of providing public services shall do so in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and the provisions of the relevant competent departments or institutions of the State Council. The competent department of national government information disclosure work may formulate special provisions based on actual needs.
If a public enterprise or institution specified in the preceding paragraph fails to disclose information produced or obtained in the process of providing public services in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and the provisions of the relevant competent departments or institutions of the State Council, a citizen, legal person, or any other organization may petition to the relevant competent department or institution, and the department or institution accepting the petition shall promptly investigate and handle the matter and inform the petitioner of the result.
Article 56 These Regulations shall come into force as of May 15, 2019.
